elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Subparagraphs 7.1 and 7.2 are retained unchanged: Capital Costs and O&M Costs "shall be borne by the Parties in the proportions set forth in Schedule B", so a fixed proportional cost commitment survives; the inserted 7.2A only caps its duration and permits reduction rather than eliminating it.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: No usage- or order-based payment basis is introduced; our obligation remains a Schedule B proportional share of consortium Capital and O&M Costs irrespective of capacity actually used.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted 7.2A: "Teleglobe USA Inc.'s commitment to bear Capital Costs and O&M Costs under Subparagraphs 7.1 and 7.2 is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period" — expressly displaces the open-ended 25-year exposure under 18.1 for cost-bearing purposes.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted 7.2A: "Teleglobe USA Inc. may reduce that commitment, and its Investment Share in Schedule B, on thirty (30) days' written notice to the Management Committee" — an unconditional election, not subject to Management Committee approval or unanimity under 18.2.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Inserted 7.2A: "Any shortfall resulting from such reduction shall be settled by a true-up of costs actually incurred and allocated, and not by any penalty, forfeiture or reclamation of capacity" — a true-up mechanic that expressly displaces the 23.2 forfeiture/reclamation consequence for the shortfall created by the reduction.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Conditional/not applicable at the preferred level: the preferred position contemplates no commitment at all, so no shortfall mechanic is required there. Recorded for completeness only; the preferred level still fails on its two own elements.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted subparagraph 7.2A delivers all three fallback elements in operative language — a 12-month cap on the cost commitment, a unilateral 30-day reduction right, and true-up (not penalty/forfeiture) settlement of the resulting shortfall.
Preferred is correctly not claimed: 7.1 and 7.2 still impose a fixed Schedule B proportional share of Capital and O&M Costs, and nothing ties payment to usage or ordered services.

Deviation classification is sound. As drafted the contract sits in walk-away territory: a 25-year Initial Period commitment (18.1) with no pre-term exit, no credit for capital costs on termination, and reclamation of capacity with no payment, credit or reimbursement (23.2) — i.e. multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, and favourable retained language (13.2, 14.1 no forced upgrade funding; 18.1 one-year notice right) is preserved. The Investment Share/Schedule B reference is operationally necessary because 7.1-7.2 allocate costs by Schedule B proportions, and the "forfeiture or reclamation of capacity" wording is necessary to prevent the retained 23.2 penalty mechanic from re-importing a shortfall penalty; neither is a gratuitous extra.

Intent preserved: the reduction right is drafted as a Teleglobe-only right, so other Parties cannot shed share onto us; billing, Management Committee governance, default and realisation-of-assets mechanics otherwise survive. The insertion works by direct amendment of 7.1-7.2 rather than a broad notwithstanding override.

Drafting improvement (not a completeness failure): "the then-current twelve (12) month period" has no stated anchor. Anchor it to the annual billing/cost period or to successive twelve-month periods from the RFS Date so the cap cannot be argued to be indeterminate.

Residual tension to watch (not fatal): 23.2 still permits reclamation of capacity for a defaulting Party generally. 7.2A only disapplies reclamation for "any shortfall resulting from such reduction". If the counterparty may argue a post-reduction allocation dispute is a payment default, consider widening to "any shortfall in Teleglobe USA Inc.'s Investment Share or cost contribution" so the true-up is the exclusive remedy.
